positive_emotions.definition: So into something (a game, book, project) that the rest of the world fades out for a while.
Okay with how things are — people, situations, yourself — without fighting reality every second.
Willing to adjust and make room for others so things can work for everyone.
That "I actually did it" feeling after finishing something that took real effort.
You can roll with change — new school, new plan, surprise problem — without totally falling apart.
Usually negative: treating people like opponents you have to beat. Odd on this list.
Easy to get along with; you are willing to cooperate instead of picking fights.
Switched on — noticing what is happening around you and ready to respond.
You care about helping others even when there is nothing in it for you.
You break problems into pieces and think them through logically.
You look at someone or something and think, "Yeah, that is good / that works."
Real — you are not faking a personality to impress people.
Not living in extremes; work, rest, emotions, and relationships feel steadier.
Seeing or feeling beauty — in art, nature, a moment, or even yourself.
You do the right or hard thing even when you are scared.
Settled inside — not revved up, not panicking; your nervous system is chill.
Upbeat mood; you bring a little light into the room.
You feel with people who are hurting and want to help, not just stare.
You trust you can handle stuff — or at least try without collapsing.
Not chasing more every second; you are okay with what you have right now.
You work with people instead of against them.
Same family as brave — stepping up when it costs you something.
You make new ideas, art, solutions, or jokes that did not exist before.
You actually want to know how things work and why people do what they do.
You carry yourself with self-respect — not sloppy, not desperate for approval.
A little weird in your own unique way — and you are fine with that.
Over-the-top happy — like winning something huge or hearing the best news ever.
You can feel what someone else might be feeling, not just your own side.
You believe you have real say in your life and can make things happen.
Amped up in a good way — something good is coming or happening.
You let your feelings and thoughts show — through words, art, humor, whatever.
You get energy from people; being around others charges you up.
You try to be even-handed — not playing favorites or bending rules for yourself.
Loyal and steady — you stick to people, promises, or beliefs you have committed to.
Happy about something specific — "I am glad you came," "glad that is over."
You notice what is good and actually appreciate it instead of taking it for granted.
General good mood — life feels lighter and more pleasant.
You jump in to make someone's load easier when you can.
Usually negative: holding back because you are unsure or scared. Odd on this list.
You believe things should be better and you care about big values like justice or truth.
You think for yourself and do not just copy the crowd to fit in.
Something sparked you — an idea, person, song — and now you want to do something.
Something catches your attention and you want to learn or engage more.
You look inward — thinking about your motives, patterns, and what you really feel.
Feeling like nothing can touch you — strong, protected, untouchable. (Can be real confidence or denial.)
Deep, bright happiness — not just "fine," but genuinely glad to be alive.
People enjoy being around you; you are pleasant without being fake.
Full of energy and spark; you animate a room.
You feel cared for and valued by someone — not alone in that way.
You are giving care, warmth, and loyalty to others.
You help two sides calm down and find middle ground instead of escalating.
Willing to hear new ideas, feelings, and experiences without slamming the door.
You care hard about something — a cause, person, hobby, goal.
Inner quiet — little internal war, even if the outside world is noisy.
Satisfied with how something turned out — a grade, a conversation, a meal.
You feel capable and influential — like your choices actually matter.
You focus on what actually works in real life, not just cool theories.
Healthy pride: you are glad about something you did or who you are becoming.
Your life feels like it is going somewhere that means something.
Celebrating hard — gratitude and happiness spilling out.
You own your duties and follow through on what you said you would do.
You are okay being you — flaws included — without constant self-attack.
You pick up on vibes and feelings (yours and others') — can be a strength.
Deep calm — like a still lake inside you.
The state of that calm — quiet steadiness.
Emotions and life do not feel like a roller coaster every hour.
Your brain is engaged and awake — interested, challenged, alive.
You can live alongside differences — opinions, styles, backgrounds — without freaking out.
You get where someone is coming from, even if you disagree.
Not worried or bothered — either healthy chill or not caring when you should. (Depends.)
You see possibilities others miss — future ideas, big dreams, new paths.
Your intentions are good even if you sometimes mess up the execution.
You have learned from life and give advice or choices that actually hold up over time.
You feel you deserve respect, love, and a place in the world — not garbage.
You are oriented toward helping others, not just yourself.
You feel your life and role matter — you are not invisible.

positive_attitudes.definition: Willingness to receive people and reality as they are instead of constantly rejecting.
You can hear different opinions without treating disagreement as war.
Warm and closeness-oriented — hugs, kind words, gentle energy.
You want to grow, achieve, and reach higher — you are not satisfied staying small.
You are reaching toward a better version of yourself or a goal you care about.
Honest and direct — you say what you mean without sneaky games.
You look out for people's well-being; their pain matters to you.
Openness to growth and new ways — you do not need everything frozen forever.
Bright, friendly default mood that lifts the people around you.
You think about how your actions land on others before you act.
Team-player mindset — shared win over solo glory.
Willing to face fear, speak up, or do hard things when it counts.
You can pick a direction and commit instead of spinning forever.
Once you decide, you keep pushing even when it gets ugly.
Loyal and all-in toward someone or something you have pledged yourself to.
You welcome experiences, people, or truth instead of dodging them.
You can keep going through boredom, pain, or delay without quitting immediately.
Genuinely pumped — your energy shows you care.
Big-hearted and open — room for ideas, people, and possibilities.
Trust in God, people, process, or hope — believing good can hold even when you cannot see it yet.
You bend when plans change instead of snapping.
You lock in on what matters and do not drift every five seconds.
You release grudges and let people (including yourself) move forward after hurt.
Valuing the ability to choose, grow, and not be controlled — for you and others.
Approachable and kind toward people; you do not act like everyone is an enemy.
Smart with money and time — not wasteful, not reckless.
You give — time, money, attention, credit — without hoarding everything.
You want good for others, not harm; basic "I am on your side" energy.
Habit of noticing and thanking for what is good in life.
You show up and put in effort even when motivation dips.
Truth is your default — you do not build your life on lies.
You know you are not the center of the universe; you can learn and apologize.
You participate — you do not sit on the sidelines of your own life or community.
You treat people with gentleness and respect, especially when you could be harsh.
You have inner drive pushing you toward goals.
You can celebrate others' wins without secretly wanting to tear them down.
Willing to consider ideas that are not yours yet.
You expect things can work out — not blind, but hopeful.
Keep-going grit when everything says stop.
You look for solutions and good possibilities instead of drowning in doom.
Feet-on-the-ground thinking — what will actually work Monday morning?
You respect time — yours and others' — by showing up when you said you would.
You see things as they are, not only as you wish they were.
People can count on you to do what you said.
You own your role, mistakes, and duties.
When someone reaches out, you answer — you do not ghost the people who matter.
You trust your ability to learn, decide, and handle life.
You steer your choices — not just parents, trends, or fear.
You can delay gratification and stick to rules you chose.
Healthy sense that you have value even when you fail a test or lose a friend.
You invest yourself for others' good, not only your comfort.
You consider others' needs alongside (or before) your own when it matters.
You can stand on your own feet and solve problems without always needing a rescue.
Attuned to feelings and atmosphere — you notice what others miss.
You take important things seriously instead of joking through everything.
What you say matches what you mean — no performance personality.
You are okay being yourself in groups; you do not need everyone's approval to function.
You feel for people who are struggling and show it.
You think before you speak or act; you consider impact.
Specifically aimed at not being careless with people's hearts.
You give people reasonable benefit of the doubt instead of assuming the worst.
Live-and-let-live toward differences that do not require war.
No fake "I am better than you" act — down-to-earth.
You do not hog everything — spotlight, resources, last slice — for yourself.
Ready to try, help, change, or show up when asked.
You value effort and getting things done over pure vibes.
Engaged with learning and people — curiosity as a lifestyle.
Usually negative: keeping emotional space on purpose. Odd on this list.
Negative: dark, pessimistic mood. Definitely misplaced here.
The attitude that "this is mine to carry" — ownership of your part in life.

negative_emotions.definition: Hurting someone on purpose with words, actions, or control — a pattern, not one bad day.
Coming at people hard — yelling, shoving, intimidation, win-at-all-costs energy.
Hot, fired-up feeling when something feels unfair, blocked, or disrespectful.
Mild irritation — the pencil tap, the repeat question, the slow walker.
Almost looking for conflict; you poke bears on purpose.
Worried and on edge about what might go wrong; body might feel tight or shaky.
Acting like you are above everyone and their opinions are worthless.
Feeling like you are bad or broken, not just that you messed up once.
Hostile and ready to fight; will not stand down easily.
Old hurt that turned into ongoing resentment you keep chewing on.
Nothing feels worth your attention; you are unstimulated and stuck.
Emotionally or mentally exhausted — like you hit a wall.
Repeatedly targeted, mocked, or pushed around by someone with more power in that setting.
Life or your head feels messy, unpredictable, out of control.
Emotionally shut off; little warmth or connection toward others.
Bossing people around and expecting obedience.
Everything is a contest; beating others matters more than doing well.
Fixating on what is wrong over and over without fixing anything.
Too in love with yourself; you think you are the main character everywhere.
Feeling judged, guilty, and like you deserve punishment with no way out.
Pulled two ways inside — want one thing, want the opposite too.
Do not understand what is happening, what you feel, or what to do.
On this list: rigid, resistant to change — "my way / the old way only."
Someone else runs your choices; you feel you have little say.
You micromanage people and situations because fear says you must.
Fear wins; you avoid doing what you know is right or needed.
Always spotting flaws — in yourself, others, everything — harshly.
Willing to hurt people, sometimes for your own satisfaction.
Already feel like you lost; trying seems pointless.
Believing things that are not true and not seeing reality clearly.
Expecting a lot and getting upset when it is not delivered.
Leaning on someone else for worth, decisions, or stability in an unhealthy way.
Ongoing sadness, emptiness, low energy, little hope — more than a bad day.
So scared or needy you will do almost anything to fix the feeling.
Feeling completely empty inside — nothing left in the tank spiritually or emotionally.
You damage relationships, future, or self — on purpose or without caring.
Checked out emotionally; present in body, not in connection.
Not linked to people, purpose, or your own feelings.
Motivation got knocked down; hard to believe things improve.
Strong "this is gross/wrong/unbearable" reaction.
Someone overpowers you; you feel small under their influence.
You overpower others so they submit to you.
World revolves around you; others' needs barely register.
Big ego — need admiration, think you are above most people.
Want what someone else has and resent that they have it.
Mood or behavior swings unpredictably; people cannot count on you.
Scared something bad is coming or happening.
Blocked from a goal; irritated because nothing is working.
Normally positive — probably misplaced on this list.
Always wanting more — stuff, attention, control — never satisfied.
Deep sadness after loss — death, breakup, big life change.
Intense ongoing hostility toward someone or something.
Cannot see how anything could improve; future looks dark.
Do not know what you need to know — never learned or refused to learn.
Hate waiting; want results now; get irritated when life is slow.
Feeling spiritually or emotionally broke — empty inside.
Act on first urge without thinking about consequences.
Do not care much either way; nothing really matters.
Frozen and unmoving — cannot get yourself going.
Doubt your value; worry constantly what others think.
Do not notice or care how your words or actions hit others.
Do not own choices; dodge duties; let others clean up.
Low-level "ugh" — things getting on your nerves.
Alone in a way that hurts; do not feel you belong.
Afraid of losing someone or something to a rival; insecurity mixed in.
Feel like others are watching and condemning you.
Quick to label people wrong or less-than without grace.
Avoid effort when you know you should move; choose easy over necessary.
Alone and hurting — even in a crowd, not truly connected.
No direction; do not know who you are or where you are going.
Really angry — might explode or simmer hard.
Someone steers you through guilt, lies, charm, or pressure.
You twist people or situations to get what you want instead of being straight.
Deeply unhappy most of the time; life feels heavy.
Emotional weather changes fast; people walk on eggshells.
Usually positive — here may mean preachy or rigid about rules.
Default to the bad side — expect failure, drama, worst outcomes.
Usually positive — here may mean acting superior or self-righteous.
One thing takes over your mind and will not let go.
Sudden intense fear — heart racing, cannot think straight.
Convinced people are against you without solid proof.
Let life happen; do not speak up or act when you should.
Nothing is ever good enough; small flaw equals total failure.
Feel so weak or sad you (or others) see you as someone to pity.
Feeling lacking — not enough support, resources, or inner strength.
Treat a person like property you control, not a free human.
Mind stuck on one worry or topic; cannot be present.
Putting off what you need to do until last minute or never.
Feel like you are paying for something — by life, people, or guilt.
Hurt others (or yourself) as payback.
Anger so intense it is almost uncontrollable.
Respond instantly without thinking — blow up or shut down.
Pull away from people; hide from the world.
Feel unwanted, excluded, not chosen.
Push feelings or memories down so hard you barely know they are there.
Hold onto anger about how you were treated; will not let go.
Given up fighting for change — "this is just how it is."
Usually positive — here may mean carrying guilt for everything, even what is not your fault.
Feel foolish or embarrassed like a joke — or treat others that way.
Here: self-righteous — morally superior, looking down on others.
Crush people or rules to get what you want; no mercy.
Down, hurt, sorrowful — often with tears or heaviness.
Get pleasure from hurting or humiliating someone — serious red flag.
Hide a lot; people cannot really know you.
Attack yourself in your head — "I am terrible, I ruin everything."
Sabotage your own success without meaning to.
Hurt yourself (risky behavior, burning bridges) because pain feels familiar.
Genuinely dislike or hate who you are.
Most thoughts are about you — image, pain, drama.
"Poor me" — wallow instead of moving forward.
Wreck opportunities right when things could go well.
Put your wants first most of the time; little room for others.
Public humiliation feeling — exposed as bad.
Emotionally numb; closed the door on feeling because it hurt too much.
Uncomfortable around people; hold back from fear of judgment.
Here: guilt or worthlessness ("I am sorry I exist"), not apologizing.
Hit hard by grief, shock, or guilt — wind knocked out of you.
Wired, exhausted, overwhelmed — stress, no sleep, or substances.
Will not bend even when wrong or when compromise would help.
Act above others — smarter, better, more important.
Meltdown when you do not get your way — yelling, throwing, dramatic shutdown.
Scared to speak up or take risks; shrink back.
Do not care about things that probably should matter.
Hold grudges; will not release what someone did.
Baseline mood is down; not satisfied with life.
Do not react when people reach out — emotionally unavailable.
Assume people will hurt, lie, or disappoint you.
Obsessed with how you look or how others see you.
Want to get even — hurt them back.
Mean in a sharp, attacking way — meant to wound.
Feel life or people keep doing you wrong and you have no power.
Physical or verbal aggression that can harm someone.
Normally positive — probably misplaced on this list.

negative_attitudes.definition: Acting fake or overly dramatic to get reactions.
Cool, distant, uninterested — hard to approach on purpose.
"Whatever" — do not invest care or effort in much.
Attitude that you are above others.
"My way or the highway" — demand obedience.
Hard-hearted; others' pain does not move you.
Gloomy outlook; rarely bring light.
Not open to new ideas, people, or feedback.
Distant and unfeeling toward others.
Treat conversations like battles to win.
Comfortable staying mediocre; will not push to grow.
Think highly of yourself in a show-off way.
Tight, limited thinking or living — no room to breathe or change.
Need to run situations and people to feel okay.
Only show up or care when it is easy or benefits you.
Want what belongs to others — stuff, status, relationships.
Shrink back in fear instead of standing up when it matters.
Harsh and hurtful as a default stance.
Lie, hide truth, or mislead on purpose.
Lean on others for everything instead of building your own footing.
Others, trends, or pressure decide your choices — not your values.
Bend or break truth to protect yourself or get ahead.
Messy habits, chaotic life — things fall apart around you.
Cannot track time, tasks, priorities; always scrambling.
Emotionally far; people do not feel close to you.
Everything revolves around you.
Resent others for what they have that you want.
Fear drives most decisions; expect danger or failure.
Running out of steam — effort and enthusiasm fading.
Do not stick with things; commitment lasts minutes.
Quit when it gets hard instead of pushing through.
Irritable; small things set you off.
Walls up so nobody gets too close.
Settled hostility toward someone or something.
Unfriendly, ready for conflict; people feel unsafe.
Wish bad things for someone; root against them.
Act younger than your age — dodge responsibility, drama, selfishness.
Rude manners — interrupt, disrespect, no basic courtesy.
Chase ideas that do not work in real life.
Do not think about how your actions affect others.
Cannot pick a direction; fear of wrong choice paralyzes you.
Act like nothing and no one matters.
Let yourself (or others) overdo bad habits without limits.
Will not adapt when plans change.
Do not trust yourself; need constant reassurance.
Blow past others' feelings without noticing.
Fake nice — say what people want, do not mean it.
Refuse to hear other sides.
Cannot accept differences — opinions, backgrounds, beliefs.
Guard what is "yours"; constantly compare to rivals.
Assume people will fail or betray you.
Do not believe you can handle life or grow.
Doubt your abilities; hold back.
Disrespect time by always running behind.
Avoid effort; choose easiest path every time.
Dishonesty as habit — spin truth to escape or control.
Intend harm — want someone to suffer.
Put people down, exclude, or hurt for sport.
Stingy with money, time, kindness, or credit.
Suspect people's motives without good reason.
Small-minded — only accept your bubble of ideas and people.
Filter life through "this will fail" glasses.
Your approach does not work long-term; collapses under pressure.
Expect the worst as default.
Sweat small stuff; hold tiny grudges.
Act fancy or important to impress.
No consistency; people cannot rely on you.
Oppose authority just to oppose — rules feel like the enemy.
New ideas or routines threaten you, so you block them.
Give in to pressure even when you know better — or wear others down until they cave.
Drag feet; participate without heart.
Stockpile old wrongs and replay them.
Schedules, opinions, habits set in stone — no bend.
Disrespectful in how you talk to and treat people.
Pulled too many directions; cannot focus or finish.
Hide big parts of life from people who should trust you.
Your needs and story sit in the center.
Think you are already good enough; stop improving.
Your gain first, even at others' expense.
Judge quickly, think small, reject outside comfort zone.
Change yourself to fit in; cannot stand being disliked.
Bitter attitude that poisons the mood.
Do not answer or engage when people need you.
No self-control — say or do whatever pops up.
Second-guess everything; hesitate until you stall.
Habits or mindset burn you out instead of building you up.
Do not offer understanding when someone struggles.
Walls up; expect betrayal.
Refuse to try, change, or cooperate even when it would help.
Obsessed with appearance, status, or being admired.
Blow time, money, energy, or opportunities without valuing them.
